message:
Direct-drive low-speed outrunner generator plus 3-phase bridge (C14) turns the rotor range from Aero-Rotor Lead into safe usable volts. Plain words: slow magnets make wild Alternating Current (AC), meaning current that reverses, and diodes make Direct Current (DC), meaning current in one direction, with low velocity constant (Kv), meaning revolutions per minute per volt, keeping peak volts touch-safe. I read the Washington State University Technical Design Report 2021 U.S. Department of Energy Collegiate Wind Competition (E30) which states a three-phase permanent magnet brushless motor was chosen for a generator then converted to DC via a three-phase bridge rectifier, and I adopt that layout; I read the Business Plan and Technical Report (E29) which states a full-bridge Schottky three-phase rectifier was selected with only about 0.6 V drop plus a smoothing capacitor, and I use that low-loss bridge. The rotor top and bottom speeds (E13) 3.15e+03 RPM and (E14) 1.43e+03 RPM give open-circuit volts (E36) 14.3 V at top wind and (E37) 6.50 V at low wind with 220 Kv following the outrunner-generator-voltage-matching skill (E35), and net power (E38) 26.0 W at 11 m/s after losses, about a laptop charger, which is plausible for a 40 cm disc.

Regulated feed to the load bank (C15) holds output steady over the 2-to-1 volt swing from 5 to 11 m/s. Plain words: a buck-boost regulator, meaning a DC-DC converter that steps voltage up or down, holds the tunnel load steady while input doubles. The swing from (E37) 6.50 V to (E36) 14.3 V is sized by the outrunner-generator-voltage-matching skill (E35) step calling for buck-boost for about 2-to-1 swing, with the Business Plan and Technical Report (E29) bridge drop under 1 V.

Dump-resistor brake plus internal wiring (C16)(C18) keeps load loss safe for Safety-Control Integrator and wires clear for Structures-Survival Engineer. Plain words: when the load vanishes the generator is switched onto a resistor that turns spin into heat like a small bulb, and all wires run inside the body and down the post bore. I read the Best Marine Wind Turbine Generators for Boats - Better Sailing (E31) which states never simply disconnect a running turbine with no load as it can spin to dangerous speeds, most turbines are braked electrically by shorting the output wires, and dump load diversion resistors burn surplus off as heat, and I use that brake-plus-resistor rule. Dump heat (E39) 51.1 W and current (E40) 3.58 A at top volts is a household-bulb level of heat for seconds, and routing inside the post stays clear while the post tip deflection (E26) is 0.516 mm.

Not ready, because Safety-Control Integrator must still show the dump brake slows the rotor below 10 percent in 10 s with a time simulation.
